sentences.text: The fossil record of Yuanmousaurus consists of nine back bones, three hip bones, and seven tail vertebrae.
Measurements show the upper arm bone was 0.72 times the length of the thigh bone.
The single known specimen, catalogued as YMV 601, was gathered in May 2000 near the village of Jiangyi in Yunnan Province.
Scientists Lü Junchang and colleagues officially named the species Yuanmousaurus jiangyiensis in 2006.
This animal lived roughly 165 million years ago during the Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic in Asia.
Its existence spanned from 174.7 to 161.5 million years ago, covering the Aalenian and Callovian stages.
Experts debate whether Yuanmousaurus represents a valid genus, as some consider it a dubious classification.
